threads.thread_goal: Align on current workflow, main pain points and pilot scope for one aisle.

messages.text: Hi team, let's kick off the 'Store Backroom-to-Shelf Replenishment Optimisation Pilot'. To start, can everyone briefly describe the current process from their perspective? We need to map the existing workflow for T1. What are the biggest delays or problems you face today?

From my side, the main issue is when pallets arrive poorly stacked. We have to break them down in the aisle which blocks customers and takes a lot of time. Also, sometimes the paperwork from the backroom doesn't match what's actually on the pallet.
For us movers, it's mostly about getting the pallets to the right aisle. Sometimes the aisles are blocked by cleaning carts or empty boxes from the last shift. It causes a traffic jam.

I agree with @321832 on the paperwork. I've started a draft of the current workflow in A1 based on my observations, but it needs your input to be accurate. The handoff between movers and fillers seems to be a key friction point.

Thanks, this is great input. It confirms the need for a standardized process. Let's choose a pilot aisle. Given the issue with mixed, heavy pallets, I suggest Aisle 7 with canned goods and dry pasta. It's high-volume and a good test for our new process.
Aisle 7 is a good choice. It's one of the worst for clutter and restocking delays. If we can fix that one, the process should work anywhere.
Aisle 7 works for me. The pallets are heavy but it's a straight shot from the backroom door.
where is the A1 doc?
I'll pin the link to the channel, @300804. It's in our shared drive.
Excellent, we have consensus. Let's lock that in. D1: The pilot will focus on Aisle 7 (Canned Goods & Dry Pasta).

Now for timing. The project must be completed within 21 days. I propose we start the pilot this coming Monday and run it for 10 full working days. This gives us a week for prep and a week for analysis afterwards.
That works. It gives me enough time to finalize the shift allocation plan for T6. I'll have the draft of A6 ready for review by EOD tomorrow.
Sounds good. We have a big delivery on Monday, so it will be a good first test.
Monday is fine.
ok
Perfect. Decision made then. D2: The pilot will start next Monday and run for 10 working days. I'll update the main project file. Great start everyone.

Just to add, for T1, a big pain point from the office side is tracking down who signed for a delivery when there's a discrepancy. The paperwork often gets misplaced between the backroom and the office.
Good point. Let's make sure our new process addresses a clear sign-off step. I've added it as a note to the T1 documentation in A1.

threads.thread_goal: Define and validate the new loading, movement and shelf routines.

messages.text: Hi all, as promised, here are the first drafts for the new standardized routines. Please find A2 (Standard Loading and Movement Sequence) and A4 (Shelf Replenishment Routine) attached. Appreciate your feedback so we can finalize T2 and T4.

Thanks @37492. A4 looks great, the steps for stock rotation and checking shelf life are very clear. For A2, I'd strongly suggest we add a rule: 'heavy items (e.g., cases of cans) must always be placed at the bottom of trolleys/pallets'. It's a huge safety risk when they're stacked on top of lighter goods.

Yes, good point. We try to do that but sometimes things are rushed. Having it as a rule is good. Also, what about cleaning? We need to make sure the cleaning schedule doesn't clash with our main replenishment times. That's part of T10 right?

Excellent points from both of you. @321832, that safety rule is critical. Let's add it. @36271, you're right to bring up T10. The routines in A2 and A4 must account for other store activities. Let's add a step: 'Confirm aisle is clear of other activities (e.g., cleaning) before entry'.
Great feedback. I've updated both A2 and A4 with those changes. I'll also coordinate with the cleaning supervisor to get their schedule and make sure it's posted in the backroom as part of T10.
the documents look ok to me
Perfect. The updated versions look ready for the pilot.
Looks good.

Alright, let's make it official. We are approving the updated routines for the pilot. D3: The standard loading and movement sequence in A2 is approved. D4: The shelf replenishment routine in A4 is approved. Thanks @37492 for the quick turnaround.
No problem! Glad we could lock this in before the weekend.

On the cleaning topic for T10, we should also make sure the cleaning team knows not to leave wet floor signs in the middle of the aisle during stocking hours. It's a tripping hazard when we're carrying boxes.
Yeah, or when I'm using the forklift.
Valid safety concern. @37492, please include this point in your discussion with the cleaning supervisor for T10.
Will do. I've added it to my notes for the meeting.

threads.thread_goal: Lock in safety, hygiene and incident logging practices for the pilot.

messages.text: Team, let's finalize our safety and tracking documents. I've created a draft for A3 (Safety and Hygiene Checklist) and A7 (Incident and Exception Log). Please review and comment so we can complete T3 and T9. The goal is to make them simple and quick to use during a busy shift.

The checklist A3 looks good. It covers the main points like safe lifting and checking for spills. For the incident log A7, can we have a pre-defined list of common issues? Like 'Damaged Packaging', 'Incorrect Item', 'Safety Hazard'. It would be faster than writing it out each time.

That's a great idea. It will also make it easier to categorize and count the incidents later. I can add a dropdown in the sheet for that. I'll also make sure the checklist A3 is printed on laminated paper and available in the backroom and on Aisle 7.
The checklist is fine. For the log, when do we fill it out? Right when it happens? Sometimes we are too busy.

Good question, @36271. For safety incidents, they must be logged immediately. For other things like damaged packaging, you should log it as soon as you have a moment, but definitely before the end of your shift. We need to capture the data while it's fresh.
who is going to check the checklist?
The shift supervisor should do spot checks, but it's on all of us to use it for our own tasks. It's about building a habit. This is part of T12, validating that we're following the process.
Exactly right, @321832. It's a self-check tool first and foremost. Okay, based on the feedback, @37492 will update A7 with pre-defined categories. Any other comments on A3?
No, A3 is good.
Update done on A7. The new version with the dropdown is live.

Fantastic. Let's finalize these. D5: The final version of the safety and hygiene checklist A3 is confirmed. D6: Staff must fill in the incident log A7 immediately for safety issues, and before end-of-shift for all other issues.
I'll take on T3 and T9 to ensure the final documents are distributed and everyone is briefed before Monday's pilot start.
I'll make sure the evening shift team knows the process for the log as well.

threads.thread_goal: Coordinate daily execution, tracking and quick fixes during the pilot.

messages.text: Pilot Day 1 is a go! :rocket: This thread is for our daily updates. Please post a quick summary at the end of your shift: what went well, any issues, and anything the next shift needs to know. Remember to log all data in A5 and any incidents in A7.
First delivery is done. The new loading sequence from A2 felt a bit slow at first but we didn't have any issues. Aisle was clear, no problems with cleaning crew. T7 is underway.

Day shift report for T8: Replenishment on Aisle 7 was much smoother. Having the pallets properly stacked made a huge difference. We filled the shelves about 15% faster than usual. I've logged the times and shelf condition in A5. No incidents to report in A7.
That's great news! I'm monitoring the tracking sheet A5 and the data looks clean so far. How often should we be updating it? After each pallet, or end of shift?

Good question. To keep it simple, let's have the on-floor team update A5 at the end of their replenishment cycle for that aisle. For status updates here, a single post at the end of each shift is perfect. Let's make that the official process.
Works for me. End of cycle for the sheet, end of shift for the channel update.
Great. D7: The tracking sheet A5 will be updated at the end of each replenishment cycle, and a status summary will be posted in this channel at every shift change.
I checked the shift plan A6 and everyone is here.
Ok, got it.
Thanks for confirming, @300804. Please continue to monitor T5 and ensure the tracking sheet is being filled correctly.
Evening shift update: One minor issue. A case of tomato sauce was dropped and damaged during movement. I've logged it in A7. We cleaned it up right away. Otherwise, the process is still working well.
Thanks for logging it promptly, @321832. This is exactly why we have the log. We can see if there's a pattern.

threads.thread_goal: Review pilot results and agree on next steps and improvements.

messages.text: Team, we've reached the end of our 10-day pilot. A huge thank you to everyone for your hard work! @37492 has consolidated the data from A5 and A7 into a summary report, A8. Please take a look. Let's discuss the results and decide on next steps.

The summary A8 is ready. Key highlights: replenishment time for Aisle 7 decreased by an average of 22%, shelf gaps were down by 40%, and we had only 3 minor incidents logged in A7 over the two weeks. The full data is in A5. This looks like a big success.

The numbers feel right. It was definitely faster and safer. The biggest win was the standardized pallet stacking. I think we should keep this process for Aisle 7 permanently and think about rolling it out to other aisles.
It was better for us too. Less confusion. I agree we should keep doing it this way. Maybe we can do Aisle 5 (beverages) next? That one is also heavy.
Great to hear the positive feedback from the floor. It seems we have a clear consensus to keep the changes. The question is how we expand. Do we go aisle by aisle, or do a bigger rollout?

Based on the pilot, I'd suggest expanding to two more aisles next month - maybe one heavy goods like Aisle 5 and one with mixed goods like Aisle 3 (snacks and confectionery). This would let us test the process on different product types before a full store rollout.
the report looks good
I like that phased approach. It lets us learn and adapt without disrupting the whole store at once.
I agree. A phased rollout is the smart way to go. Let's formalize this. D8: We will make the new process permanent for Aisle 7 and expand the pilot to Aisles 3 and 5 next month.
I will take T11 and write up the final proposal with these recommendations to share with the store operations manager. Thanks again everyone for a successful pilot!
Sounds good. Let us know when we start the next one.
